claim: A menu line read sends its raw line (menu_items.raw_extracted_text, for a CSV the whole row with every unmapped cost, supplier and margin cell; csv-parser.service.ts:55) only where the caller's view allows it. menu-line-view.ts: seesRawLine needs BOTH 'money' and 'suppliers' in policyFor's ROLE_POLICY row (ADR 0145), with no shortcut; lineForViewer copies only MEMBER_LINE_KEYS (which do not name the raw line) and assigns the raw line only inside `if (view.rawLine)`. menus.service.ts: getMenu, readLines and getVersion each default to { rawLine: false }, and readLines maps every row through lineForViewer. menus.controller.ts: GET /menus/:restaurantId passes { rawLine: false } for every viewer and GET /menu-versions/:menuId passes { rawLine: seesRawLine(role) } from the token's role; arrival.service.ts's one getMenu call passes { rawLine: false }. Checks the shape of the code, not its run: the jest cases in menus.service.spec.ts ('a line's raw line is a holder's') and menu-line-view.spec.ts check the behaviour. Not covered here: the kept source file and the import reply (see tech-debt.d/2026-10-08-fix-a-menu-line-carries-its-raw-line.md entries (i) and (iii)).

Every menu line read says kitchen_line, worked out in the gateway (lineForViewer: isKitchenLine(row.category, raw)) from the stored section and raw line, so the kitchen split does not depend on who reads; and the gateway's KITCHEN_HINTS hold the same hints as the web's KITCHEN (apps/web/src/lib/firstProof.ts), so the two tests cannot drift apart unseen.

claim: A guard on names and selects, not on behaviour.
